html:
Mai, or king, of Bornu in the late 16th century, whose wars made Kanem-Bornu the leading power around Lake Chad.

Ruling from Ngazargamu in what is now northeastern Nigeria, he hired Turkish musketeers and bought firearms through the Ottoman lands to the north, among the first such weapons in the region. He defeated the Bulala, the Sao towns and the Tuareg, made the pilgrimage to Mecca, and promoted Islamic law and courts. His imam, Ahmad ibn Furtu, wrote a chronicle of his campaigns, a rare written source from the time.
sum: Mai, or king, of Bornu in the late 16th century, whose wars made Kanem-Bornu the leading power around Lake Chad.
